behaviors.title: Select a direct, Promise, or composed response

claims.text: The dispatcher awaits each handler result, allowing synchronous return values and promises to feed the same response handling.
The HEAD wrapper awaits recursive GET dispatch and constructs a Response outside the other local handler catches. A failure in that wrapper rejects its returned Promise.
HEAD dispatch recursively uses GET as the dispatch method argument while retaining the original Request object.
The res setter replaces the new set-cookie collection with cookies from the previous response when merging that header.
The supplied outer next callback is eligible only at exactly middleware.length when no middleware entry exists.
When both old and new responses exist, the res setter copies the new response before merging old headers, skipping the old content-type.
The res getter lazily creates response storage with prepared headers; the getter itself does not set finalized.
A normal returned response does not overwrite already finalized context through this assignment condition.
The res setter stores its argument and sets finalized to true, including when the argument is undefined.
Dispatch rejects an index less than or equal to the last dispatched index with the repeated-next Error.
Zero handlers and more than one handler both enter the composition path.
The runner returns dispatch(0). This nested async function resolves to the shared context after successful completion and can reject on a propagated failure.
A truthy resolved response from that Promise is returned before consulting finalized context state.
A present middleware entry supplies its handler from middleware[i][0][0].
After awaiting onError, the dispatcher marks the result as an error response.
A non-Error throw or an Error without an onError callback is rethrown by that dispatch frame.
compose accepts middleware entries and optional error and not-found callbacks. It returns a runner that accepts a Context and optional outer next callback.
A synchronous throw from the direct handler is sent to the private error handler.
Exactly one matched handler takes a direct path that bypasses compose.
The direct path distinguishes a returned Promise using instanceof Promise.
A failure inside the awaited onError callback escapes the current frame's handler catch block.
The nested dispatch function accepts an index and closes over the runner context, progression index, middleware array, and optional callbacks.
The private dispatcher accepts a Request, execution context, environment bindings, and a method argument. The annotations do not validate runtime inputs.
The initial error callback is the local default errorHandler; its getResponse branch forwards the response body and initialization data through c.newResponse.
Outside that getResponse branch, the default error handler logs the error and requests a text response with status 500.
The handler catch uses onError only when the thrown value is an Error and an onError callback exists.
At the terminal index, a supplied outer next is invoked through handler(context, continuation). Its runtime result and effects are not established here.
The repeated-next guard throws before the current frame's handler try/catch, so that frame does not process its own guard error through onError.
A direct non-Promise result that is neither null nor undefined is returned unchanged. That expression does not check whether the value is a Response.
Before invoking onError, the handler catch writes the caught Error into context.error.
The direct-path async next callback awaits not-found, assigns the result to c.res, and has no explicit return value. It can reject if the awaited callback or assignment fails.
The onNotFound invocation is awaited outside the current handler try/catch.
Rejection in the direct Promise chain is sent to the private error handler.
Dispatch creates a Context with the request, path, match result, env, execution context, and configured not-found handler.
The Context finalized field is initialized to false.
A throw during the awaited composed path or its finalization check is passed to the private error handler.
The composition path returns context.res after checking finalized.
A falsy result does not trigger the final response assignment.
The res getter takes no explicit argument. It reads private response storage and can initialize both that storage and prepared headers.
A falsy resolved Promise value falls back to c.res when finalized, otherwise to the configured not-found handler.
A handler receives a continuation that recursively dispatches i + 1 using the same context.
For non-HEAD dispatch, the configured path resolver receives the request and an object containing env.
Router matching receives the dispatch method and the resolved path.
Selecting a middleware entry also assigns i to context.req.routeIndex.
Each invocation of the runner returned by compose initializes its own progression index to -1.
The selected source calls response constructors, header methods, and Context response helpers. Their implementations and complete failure behavior are outside these excerpts.
A non-Promise nullish direct result invokes the not-found handler; this expression does not consult c.finalized.
The runner begins asynchronous dispatch at middleware index zero.
The progression index is updated before the current handler is selected or invoked.
The res setter merges headers before its final storage assignment and finalized update. An exception during that merge can prevent those final assignments.
An unfinalized context returned by composition causes an Error about returning a Response or awaiting next.
fetch forwards the original request, its method, the environment, and the execution context into the private dispatcher.
The synchronous direct-result fallback invokes not-found outside the direct handler try/catch, so a throw there can propagate to the caller.
The dispatcher constructs compose with the matched middleware, configured error handler, and configured not-found handler.
Path resolution, route matching, and Context construction occur before the direct-handler and composed-runner try blocks. A failure there does not enter those local catches.
The direct handler receives an async next callback that assigns the configured not-found result to c.res.
The res setter accepts Response or undefined by annotation and has no explicit return value. It does not validate the argument type at runtime.
A truthy onError result may replace response state even when the context was already finalized.

If a parent handler awaits a child continuation and its rejection reaches the parent handler call, the parent frame catch can handle an Error through onError. An unawaited continuation is not guaranteed to reach that catch.
The composed frame assigns context.res after the handler catch. A failure from that assignment escapes the current handler catch and can reach an awaiting parent or application dispatcher.
Without a selected handler, onNotFound runs only when context.finalized is exactly false and the callback exists.
Eligible error callbacks receive an Error and the current context. Their returned values and failures depend on the configured implementation.
HEAD constructs a new Response with a null body and the awaited GET-dispatch response as its initialization argument.
The shown call sites supply context and a continuation to selected handlers. These excerpts do not establish their implementations, return values, failures, state changes, or use of await next().
The composition path awaits the composed runner with the newly constructed context.
The private error handler delegates Error instances to the configured error callback and rethrows other values.
A successfully completed dispatch frame returns the shared context object.
The configured not-found callback receives the current context. Its returned values and failures depend on the configured implementation.
The private error handler calls the configured error callback without a local try block. Its synchronous throw or returned rejection can pass to the caller.
A truthy response result is assigned to context.res only when context is not finalized or the result came through onError.
